sources.entry: django-cms - The easy-to-use and developer-friendly enterprise CMS powered by Django.

summary.one_liner: django CMS is an open-source, enterprise content management system built on Django, published on PyPI as the django-cms package.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains the core django-cms package, which adds page-tree content management to a Django project. It provides internationalisation (i18n) and multi-site support, front-end inline editing so editors can change rendered pages directly, and a placeholder and plugin system for reusable content components. It also offers integration with several rich-text editors, a hierarchical page tree with SEO-friendly URLs, and extensible navigation and apphooks for integrating applications. The README says content versioning, editorial workflows and headless setups come from official add-on packages rather than the core. The djangocms command can generate a configured project from the official template, or add django CMS to an existing Django project.
use_cases: add a CMS to an existing Django project
manage a hierarchical page tree with SEO URLs
run multiple sites from one installation
create reusable content plugins for pages
how_to_run: Run djangocms . in the root of an existing Django project to add django CMS to it
notable: Front-end inline editing of rendered pages
Placeholder and plugin system for reusable content components
djangocms command generates a full project from the official template
Non-profit django CMS Association backs the project
Optional headless mode and add-on packages for versioning and workflows
caveats: Content versioning, editorial workflows and headless setups depend on separate official add-on packages
Documentation and help are primarily via external sites, Discord and Stackoverflow
